The proposal was disclosed during engagements held in Cairo hosted by EGX in collaboration with the African Export-Import Bank (Afreximbank) and led by Nigerian Exchange Group Plc (NGX Group). The Cairo meeting, alongside a parallel session in Addis Ababa hosted by the Ethiopian Securities Exchange (ESX), brought together exchange leaders, financial institutions and capital market stakeholders to examine how market infrastructure and institutional partnerships can improve investment access across Africa, using the Dangote Refinery offer as a practical context. Speaking at the Cairo engagement, the executive chairman of the Egyptian Exchange, Omar Radwan highlighted the potential for EDRs to provide Egyptian investors access to selected African businesses. He expressed EGX’s readiness to work with Dangote Industries to explore a possible framework for such an arrangement. The Group managing director/CEO of NGX Group, Temi Popoola, said Africa possesses substantial pools of institutional capital but lacks the connectivity to channel it across borders. “Africa has substantial capital within its own markets, particularly across pension funds and insurance companies. The challenge is how to connect that capital to investment opportunities across the continent. The Dangote Refinery offer provides a practical opportunity to address some of the infrastructure barriers to cross-border investment. Beyond a single transaction, it is about creating connections that enable African capital to finance African growth,” Popoola said. The president and chief executive of Dangote Industries Limited, Aliko Dangote, described the refinery as an example of the scale of industrial investment required to strengthen Africa’s productive capacity, reduce dependence on imports and support long-term growth. He commended NGX Group for bringing African exchanges together around the initiative. Group chairman of NGX Group, Alhaji Umaru Kwairanga, stressed that lasting progress depends on sustained cooperation. “Our task is not simply to collaborate around one offer, but to develop lasting partnerships that support cross-border investment and capital formation across Africa. This requires cooperation among exchanges, regulators, financial institutions and businesses, alongside investment in the infrastructure and technology that make participation more accessible,” Kwairanga said. President and chairman of Afreximbank, Dr. George Elombi, reaffirmed the bank’s longstanding financing relationship with Dangote Industries and its commitment to supporting African industrial transformation. The Cairo and Addis engagements followed earlier stops at the Nairobi Securities Exchange and the Botswana Stock Exchange, extending the cross-border investment dialogue across multiple African markets.
